issues: The offer may not fit this company: Bulk school uniforms have no clear connection to Duolingo’s engineering priorities, subscription model, or app growth strategy; any link would be highly speculative.

facts.claim: Duolingo uses a freemium model: free learning is available, and paid subscriptions monetize a separate premium experience.
facts.excerpt: The freemium business model is good for our mission and our business. Duolingo started as a free product, and we remain committed to offering free learning for all while monetizing through a valuable paid experience.

facts.claim: Duolingo says product quality and experimentation are central to its strategy, with 1,000+ A/B tests per quarter.
facts.excerpt: We obsess over product quality, running 1,000+ A/B tests per quarter and refining

facts.claim: Duolingo prioritizes long-term engagement and wants users to return daily.
facts.excerpt: Instead, we focus on long-term engagement— and since motivation is the hardest part of learning, we design Duolingo to be something users want to return to daily.

facts.claim: Duolingo had 52.7M DAUs, 133.1M MAUs, and 12.2M paid subscribers as of Q4 2025.
facts.excerpt: As of Q4 2025, we have 52.7M DAUs, 133.1M MAUs, and 12.2M paid subscribers.

facts.claim: Duolingo’s paid subscription helps fund free access for millions of learners worldwide.
facts.excerpt: Your Super Duolingo subscription helps you be a superlearner — and helps us provide a free learning experience to millions of Duolingo learners worldwide.

facts.claim: Duolingo offers the Duolingo English Test, and it has been affected by U.S. Treasury sanctions-related restrictions for people testing in Iran or using Iranian government-issued ID.
facts.excerpt: Following an August 24 action by the US Treasury Department, Duolingo is required to stop offering the Duolingo English Test to people testing in Iran or using Iranian government-issued identification beginning September 1.
facts.source_title: Duolingo D-Day: Iranians question latest US sanctions targeting education | Education News | Al Jazeera

facts.claim: Duolingo’s course catalog shows very large learner counts for some subjects, including Spanish and French.

strategy.observation: Duolingo’s engineering strategy is centered on product experimentation and daily user engagement, with 1,000+ A/B tests per quarter and a goal of getting users to return every day.
strategy.offer_link: That focus makes bulk school uniforms a poor match for the VP of Engineering’s likely priorities; the offer only becomes relevant if Duolingo has an unmentioned in-person schooling or facilities need.
hypotheses: The VP of Engineering likely owns software/product infrastructure rather than procurement for physical goods.
Duolingo may not have any recurring need for school uniforms unless it runs a separate school-based or campus program not shown in the facts.
If there is a facilities or events team sourcing uniforms, engineering would not be the right first contact.
strategy.angle: Duolingo’s engineering work is about experimentation and daily engagement, so school uniforms are probably outside your remit.
strategy.fit_reason: Bulk school uniforms have no clear connection to Duolingo’s engineering priorities, subscription model, or app growth strategy; any link would be highly speculative.

draft.subject: Wrong team for uniforms
draft.body:
Hi,

I help organizations source bulk school uniforms.

Duolingo’s engineering work seems centered on experimentation and getting people back daily, with 1,000+ A/B tests per quarter. If that’s still the priority, uniforms are probably outside your remit.

If there’s a separate ops, facilities, or campus owner for purchases like this, who’s the right person for me to reach out to?
